objective: Implement a CareOps-owned idempotent multiple-birth registration contract with explicit per-recipient destinations, while documenting that fetal identity mapping is not modeled in current source.
steps: Add a typed BirthMessageId and payload that names the mother, birth event, infant ordinal/spawn/relationship event keys, maternal destination and each infant destination.

Apply a complete multiple-birth registration atomically against IdentityLedger; reject empty infant lists and validate message replay, message-ID payload conflict, unique birth event, unique infant ordinals and relationship integrity.
Return one stable person and destination intent per mother/infant; keep transfer operation ownership and failures independent per recipient.

Checkpoint and restore the birth-message ledger paired with the identity ledger; validate parent links against their original add-event records so a later explicit removal preserves valid birth history.

Document and test that current source has no fetal identity model; do not fabricate a fetal-to-newborn mapping. Keep any future mapping conditional on an explicit modeled fetal entity and provenance contract.

verification.oracle: Birth message replay is idempotent, payload/ordinal/empty-infant conflicts are atomic, multi-infant links and split destinations are retained, and restore rejects mismatched paired state while accepting a link later removed explicitly.
Core module and test targets satisfy workspace lint policy.

acceptance: BirthMessageId is distinct from BirthEventId and from Kairos or transfer message identities.
Exact birth message retry returns the original result without identity mutation; changed payload under the same message ID rejects atomically.
One birth event maps to one message; at least one infant is required, and multiple infant ordinals create distinct person identities with BirthEventId and ordinal provenance and typed mother links.
Maternal and infant destination intents can differ and are represented per person; no all-or-none multi-recipient transfer or shared failure semantics are claimed.

Paired checkpoint restore verifies birth message records against corresponding IdentityLedger people and original relationship add events; a subsequent valid relationship removal does not invalidate the birth record.
Repository source inspection and tests confirm no pre-birth fetal identity entity/API currently exists; this track records fetal mapping as not modeled rather than claiming a transition.
No Kairos source or pin, ED external schema, site policy, empirical clinical validity or operational delivery is changed or claimed.
Reviewer-agent/subagent reviews the exact integrated commit against ADR-0015 and prior A5.2 interfaces; all findings are fixed and re-reviewed before coordinator acceptance.
stop_conditions: A5.2 identity or transfer API incompatibility
Cannot make multi-infant identity and parent-link updates atomic
Fetal-to-post-birth mapping is requested without an existing modeled fetal identity or an explicit design contract
Checkpoint state cannot be validated against identity event history
Out-of-scope Kairos, ED schema or profile change
